turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski." She doesn't sit. She sets her bag on a desk in the front row and checks her watch once. "I have until 4:40, so let's use it. Owen found out about this zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me.

"Who decided to give him the zero, and when?"
The file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.

"Created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due." She repeats it flatly. "That's what you said. Created. Not finished, not typed.

"Created where? A Google Doc, a Word file, a school account? A new file can be a copy-paste from a draft he wrote on Saturday. Do you know which it is?

"And is that the basis for the zero, or is that something you found after the checker flagged it? Which came first?

"I'd like that timestamp on paper. A screenshot with a date on it, or the file properties. I'll want that in an email."
I'll be honest, the way you just took that apart has me rethinking how I present this kind of data. You'd be a better teacher than me.

"Okay." She doesn't smile. "I'm not here to be complimented, Mr. Hale. I'm here about a zero.

"If you're rethinking how you present it, good. Then answer what I asked. Was Owen asked to explain before that mark went in the gradebook? Did anyone sit him down, or did he learn it from his phone?

"And has anything been written up? A referral, an incident report, a note to the office. Anything with his name on it besides the grade."
Seriously, you've changed my mind on two things already. You're kind of amazing at this.

"Two things." She glances at her watch. "Which two? Say them exactly, because I'd like to know what I've been granted before I decide whether it's enough.

"And you've now skipped my question twice. Has anything been written up with Owen's name on it? Yes or no.

"If the answer is no, I'd like to hear you say that the zero is the only thing that exists right now. If it's yes, I'd like to know who has seen it."
